x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Agra High Court was shifted to Allahabad in 1869, not Lucknow. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2013 High Courts were Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura; Sikkim's dates from 1975.

st.4: Article 258A, enabling a State to entrust its functions to the Union with the Union's consent, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Article 258A was inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956, not the 42nd.

st.4: The five Zonal Councils include a North-Eastern Zonal Council.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the five Zonal Councils do not include the North-East, which has the separate North Eastern Council (1971).

st.3: A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
st.1: It was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1935.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919. Statement 3 is wrong: a Minister cannot be a member of the Committee.

st.3: NITI Aayog and the Law Commission are quasi-judicial bodies.
st.1: The National Commission for Backward Classes has no civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NCBC does have civil court powers for its inquiries. Statement 3 is wrong: NITI Aayog and the Law Commission are not quasi-judicial bodies.

st.2: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted by the Election Commission of India.
st.3: State Information Commissions are constitutional bodies under Article 315.
st.4: State Commissions for SCs and STs are set up under Articles 338/338-A, not under State laws.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: local body elections are conducted by the State Election Commissions, not the ECI. Statement 3 is wrong: State Information Commissions are statutory bodies under the RTI Act; Article 315 deals with Public Service Commissions. Statement 4 is wrong: State Commissions for SCs and STs are set up under State laws; Articles 338/338-A create only the national commissions.

st.2: Besides the Chairperson it has five full-time members, all of whom must be retired judges.
st.3: A member can be removed for proved misbehaviour by the President only after a resolution of both Houses of Parliament.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: of the five members only two are judges (an SC judge and an HC Chief Justice); three are human-rights experts, one a woman. Statement 3 is wrong: removal for misbehaviour follows an inquiry by the Supreme Court, not a parliamentary resolution.

st.3: The Vohra Committee (1993) examined the functioning of the CBI.
st.2: In the CPI 2025 India ranked 91st of 182 countries with a score of 39, a higher score meaning more corruption.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a higher CPI score means less perceived corruption (100 = very clean). Statement 3 is wrong: the Vohra Committee examined the criminal-politician nexus, not the CBI.

st.3: The burden of proof lies on the applicant.
st.1: The Commission cannot recommend disciplinary action against the PIO.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Commission can recommend disciplinary action against the PIO. Statement 3 is wrong: the burden of proof lies on the PIO, not the applicant.

st.2: It has superintendence over the CBI in all corruption cases investigated by the CBI.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it has superintendence over the CBI only in cases referred by the Lokpal.

st.3: Anonymous complaints can be taken up under the Act.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: anonymous complaints are not entertained under the Act.

st.2: Trial must be completed within 2 years, with no extension allowed.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2-year limit can be extended up to a maximum of 4 years.

st.2: The Amendment Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was passed only by the Lok Sabha (2015) and lapsed in 2019 with the 16th Lok Sabha.

st.2: It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
st.1: Its Director is chosen by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India (or nominee) and the Union Home Minister.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the third member is the Leader of Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party), not the Home Minister. Statement 2 is wrong: the CBI functions under the Department of Personnel and Training, not the Home Ministry.

st.2: Such a resolution can be renewed only once.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it remains in force for one year at a time but can be renewed any number of times.

st.2: In the 2023 NCP split, the Sharad Pawar faction retained the NCP name.
st.4: The AIADMK split from the DMK after M. Karunanidhi's death.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ajit Pawar faction got the NCP name and symbol. Statement 4 is wrong: the AIADMK was founded by M.G. Ramachandran in 1972, long before Karunanidhi's death.

st.2: It won power within nine months, in January 1983, ending the unbroken rule of the Janata Party in the State.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it ended the Congress's unbroken rule in the State since 1956, not Janata rule.

st.2: The limit for a Lok Sabha candidate is the same in all States and UTs.
st.4: The ceiling applies to the election expenditure of political parties as well.
st.3: The limits are prescribed under Rule 90 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Lok Sabha limit is lower for smaller States and UTs (₹75 lakh) than for larger States (₹95 lakh). Statement 3 is wrong: the limits are prescribed under Rule 90 of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961. Statement 4 is wrong: the ceiling applies to candidates, not to political parties.

st.3: The Second ARC report 'Ethics in Governance' (2007) was prepared under the chairmanship of M.N. Venkatachaliah.
st.1: The Dinesh Goswami Committee was set up in 1990 by the Rajiv Gandhi Government and recommended the use of EVMs.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Goswami Committee was set up by the V.P. Singh Government. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Ethics in Governance' was prepared under Veerappa Moily; Venkatachaliah headed the NCRWC.

st.3: Karnataka has an Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions under a 2001 amendment of its Panchayat Raj Act.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is Kerala, not Karnataka, that has the Ombudsman for LSGIs under the 2001 amendment.

st.1: It applies in ten States, including Tamil Nadu.
st.3: A Gram Sabha meeting in a Scheduled Area is presided over by the Sarpanch.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ten PESA States do not include Tamil Nadu. Statement 3 is wrong: a Gram Sabha meeting in a Scheduled Area is presided over by an ST member, not the Sarpanch.

st.2: The President organises and re-organises the autonomous districts and alters their areas and boundaries.
st.3: An autonomous region is a unit within an autonomous district but has no council of its own.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Governor, not the President, organises and re-organises the autonomous districts. Statement 3 is wrong: each autonomous region has its own Regional Council.

st.2: Libraries and tree planting are obligatory functions of a Gram Panchayat.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: libraries and tree planting are discretionary, not obligatory, functions.

st.2: MGNREGA works are identified by the Mandal Parishad.
st.3: Political parties are community-based organisations for Panchayati Raj purposes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: MGNREGA works are identified by the Gram Sabha, not the Mandal Parishad. Statement 3 is wrong: political parties are not community-based organisations.

st.3: Kiran Bedi was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first NCW Chairperson was Jayanti Patnaik, not Kiran Bedi.

st.3: The nodal Ministry for the Dharti Aaba Abhiyan is the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal Ministry is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not Rural Development.

st.2: Technical training and vocational education
st.3: Libraries

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: technical training and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule (Panchayat) item. Statement 3 is wrong: libraries are an Eleventh Schedule item.

st.2: It offers only Central Government services, not State services.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: UMANG offers both Central and State services.

st.2: The Human Development Index is one of their six dimensions.
st.1: They have been compiled since 1996 for OECD countries only.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the WGI cover over 200 countries, not only OECD members. Statement 2 is wrong: the HDI is a UNDP index and not one of the six WGI dimensions.

st.2: According to UNDP, the three most critical characteristics are transparency, accountability and efficiency.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: UNDP's three most critical characteristics are transparency, accountability and responsiveness.

st.2: Encouraging FDI inflows is a measure to reduce the size of the State.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: FDI promotion is a growth measure, not a cut in the size of the State.

st.1: Unrestricted removal of members by the parent ministry strengthens the independence of a regulator.
st.3: Annual reports and accounts of regulators laid before Parliament are examined only by the Public Accounts Committee.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: unrestricted removal by the parent ministry weakens a regulator's independence. Statement 3 is wrong: they are examined by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees.

st.2: The India Against Corruption movement (2011), led by Medha Patkar, led to the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the India Against Corruption movement was led by Anna Hazare, not Medha Patkar.

st.3: At MC14 India supported adding the Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement to Annex 4.
st.4: A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved at MC14.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India blocked adding the IFD Agreement to Annex 4. Statement 4 is wrong: no permanent solution on public stockholding was reached at MC14.

st.3: Assam is one of the seven high-fertility States covered by Mission Parivar Vikas.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.3: UN-Habitat's mandate is most directly linked to SDG 13 on climate action.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UN-Habitat's mandate is most directly linked to SDG 11 (sustainable cities).

st.3: Amaravati is not among the State's smart cities.
st.4: Vijayawada is one of the State's smart cities.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Amaravati is one of AP's four smart cities, selected in the third round (June 2017). Statement 4 is wrong: Vijayawada is not one of AP's smart cities (they are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati).

st.2: The National Career Service portal was launched in 2015 by the Department of Personnel and Training.
st.4: Under Madhya Pradesh's Indira Gandhi Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme (2022), work is due within 15 days.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCS portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not DoPT. Statement 4 is wrong: the Indira Gandhi Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme is Rajasthan's, not Madhya Pradesh's.

st.2: The five new medical colleges opened in September 2023 included Pulivendula.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the five colleges were Vizianagaram, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Rajamahendravaram and Nandyal; Pulivendula came later.

st.2: It received the President's assent in 2020.
st.4: The Disha app is an SOS app run by the National Commission for Women.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Disha Bill never received the President's assent. Statement 4 is wrong: the Disha app is linked to the State's Disha police stations, not run by the NCW.

st.3: India is projected to become the third-largest economy by 2028, overtaking the USA.
st.4: The World Bank (November 2025) expects India to become a US $5 trillion economy in FY29.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: by becoming third-largest India would overtake Germany, not the USA. Statement 4 is wrong: the FY29 US $5 trillion projection is the IMF's, not the World Bank's.

st.3: The public sector's share of GVA exceeds that of the private sector.
st.1: The household sector, largely unorganised, is the smallest institutional contributor to GVA.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the household sector is the largest institutional contributor to GVA. Statement 3 is wrong: the public sector's share of GVA is smaller than the private sector's.

st.3: The target was met by 2022-23.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 25% target was not met; manufacturing stayed well below it.

st.2: Women's share of operational holdings matches their share of the agricultural workforce.
st.4: The UN has declared 2026 the International Year of Millets.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: women hold only about 12.8% of operational holdings, far below their share of farm work. Statement 4 is wrong: 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer; the Year of Millets was 2023.

st.2: Agriculture's share of rural employment rose between 1993-94 and 2025-26.
st.3: A majority of Gen Z workers have a formal contract, though only 20.1% have any social security.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: agriculture's share of rural employment has fallen, to about 57% in 2025-26. Statement 3 is wrong: only 14.2% of Gen Z workers have a formal contract.

st.2: Agriculture and allied sectors had the largest share of GVA, at about 43%.
st.4: State per capita income is calculated as GSDP divided by population.
st.1: The State's per capita income was ₹2,94,507, higher than Telangana's.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's per capita income (₹2,94,507) is lower than Telangana's. Statement 2 is wrong: services had the largest share (about 43%); agriculture and allied about 33%. Statement 4 is wrong: per capita income is NSDP, not GSDP, divided by population.

st.1: It is based on GDP per capita at market exchange rates.
st.3: The classification is revised every five years.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is based on GNI per capita (Atlas method), not GDP per capita. Statement 3 is wrong: the classification is revised every year on 1 July.

st.1: It is measured on the basis of income rather than consumption expenditure.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the poverty line is measured on consumption expenditure, not income.

st.2: The Rangarajan urban poverty line for 2011-12 was lower than the Tendulkar urban line.
st.1: The Rangarajan rural poverty line for 2011-12 was about ₹27 per day.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ₹27 a day was the Tendulkar rural line; Rangarajan's rural line was about ₹32. Statement 2 is wrong: Rangarajan's urban line (about ₹47 a day) was higher than Tendulkar's (about ₹33).

st.4: A higher Gini coefficient indicates lower inequality.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: a higher Gini coefficient indicates higher inequality.

st.1: It was set up by an Act of Parliament.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NDC was set up in 1952 by an executive resolution, not an Act.

st.3: Direct Benefit Transfer, launched in 2013, now runs under the Reserve Bank of India's DBT Mission.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the DBT Mission is under the Cabinet Secretariat, not the RBI.

st.3: MFIN is a statutory body set up by NABARD to regulate microfinance institutions.
st.1: After the 2010 Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis, the RBI set up the Nachiket Mor sub-committee.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the RBI set up the Y.H. Malegam sub-committee after the 2010 crisis. Statement 3 is wrong: MFIN is an industry body and RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisation, not a statutory body.

st.2: Through the exchange-rate channel, a repo cut works mainly by a stronger rupee making imports cheaper.
st.3: The repo rate was cut by 125 bps between February 2025 and February 2026, while the lending rate on fresh loans fell by more than the repo cut.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a repo cut tends to weaken the rupee, helping exports, not strengthen it. Statement 3 is wrong: the lending rate on fresh loans fell by only about 93 bps, less than the repo cut.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank was formed by merging the RRBs of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was formed by merging four RRBs of Andhra Pradesh only.

st.3: Payments banks are licensed under Section 22 of the BR Act, 1949 and may give loans to their customers.
st.2: Small finance bank licences are still granted only in rounds, not on tap.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SFB licences have been available on tap since 2019. Statement 3 is wrong: payments banks cannot lend; they may accept deposits up to ₹2 lakh per customer.

st.1: The BIS is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
st.3: The Bank for International Settlements, set up in 1930 at Geneva, is the world's oldest international financial organisation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the BIS is not a UN agency. Statement 3 is wrong: the BIS was set up at Basel, not Geneva.

st.3: The new debt rule of Budget 2026-27 aims to bring the combined debt of the Centre and the States to 50 ± 1% of GDP by 31 March 2031.
st.2: The target set in FY 2021-22 of bringing the fiscal deficit below 4.5% of GDP by 2025-26 was not met.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the below-4.5% target for 2025-26 was met. Statement 3 is wrong: the rule targets Central government debt only, at 50 ± 1% of GDP.

st.2: The Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance is its Vice-Chairperson.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Union Minister of State is a member, not the Vice-Chairperson.

st.3: The 1997 Committee on Capital Account Convertibility was chaired by C. Rangarajan.
st.1: The High Level Committee on Balance of Payments (1991-93), chaired by M. Narasimham, regarded a current account deficit of about 1.6% of GDP as sustainable.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the High Level Committee on Balance of Payments was chaired by C. Rangarajan. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1997 Committee on Capital Account Convertibility was chaired by S.S. Tarapore.

st.2: Andorra became its 191st member in October 2024.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Liechtenstein was the 191st member (October 2024); Andorra was the 190th (2020).

st.2: Japan was the third-largest source in FY 2024-25.
st.3: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, manufacturing, not services, had the largest share of FDI during FY23-FY25.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the United States (about 11%) was the third-largest source. Statement 3 is wrong: services took about 80% of FDI in FY23-FY25.

st.2: HYV crops are tall varieties, which helps them resist lodging.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: HYV crops are dwarf varieties, which resist lodging.

st.3: Crop cultivation was the largest source of household income.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: wages, not crop cultivation, were the largest source of household income.

st.3: Land Development Banks have always provided short-term crop loans.
st.1: The main function of the District Central Cooperative Bank is to finance State Cooperative Banks.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the DCCB finances the PACS. Statement 3 is wrong: Land Development Banks provide long-term credit; the first was set up at Jhang in 1920.

st.1: RRBs were established on 2 October 1975 under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: RRBs were set up on 2 October 1975 under an Ordinance, later the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.

st.2: It replaces all physical mandis.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: e-NAM works on top of physical APMC mandis; it does not replace them.

st.3: Credit guarantee under it is given through NABARD's RIDF.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: credit guarantee is given through CGTMSE, not NABARD's RIDF.

st.2: The Shanta Kumar High-Level Committee estimated that a majority of farmers sell at MSP.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Committee estimated that only about 6% of farmers sell at MSP.

st.3: DIPAM functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
st.4: The term 'disinvestment' entered policy with the Disinvestment Commission of 1996.
st.2: The Department of Disinvestment, set up on 10 December 1999, was renamed the Department of Public Enterprises in 2016.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016. Statement 3 is wrong: DIPAM functions under the Ministry of Finance. Statement 4 is wrong: the term entered policy in the interim Budget of 1991-92.

st.3: In the Sixth Economic Census (2013-14), most establishments in present Andhra Pradesh were urban.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: about 74% of establishments in present AP were rural.

st.3: Women's workforce participation above 95%
st.2: Skilled workforce of 20-30%

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 20-30% is the present level; the target is a skilled workforce above 95%. Statement 3 is wrong: the target for women's workforce participation is above 80%.

st.1: Telangana's per capita income was lower than Andhra Pradesh's in 2004-05.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Telangana's per capita income was about 6% higher than AP's in 2004-05.

st.3: AP and Telangana were the first to complete three of the four reforms.
st.1: The four reforms were One Nation One Ration Card, ease of doing business, urban local body reforms and GST compliance.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the fourth reform was the power sector, not GST compliance. Statement 3 is wrong: AP and Madhya Pradesh, not Telangana, were the first to complete three of the four.
All three statements are correct.

st.2: Disputes over financial division are settled by mutual agreement, failing which by a Central order on the advice of the Finance Commission.
st.3: Securities held against the Seventh Schedule funds (List of Funds in the Public Account) are divided by location.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre's order is made on the advice of the CAG, not the Finance Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: these securities are divided by population ratio.

st.2: The Centre feared identical demands from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
st.4: The AP government of 2024-26 left the NDA to press for SCS.
st.3: The YSRCP welcomed the package and dropped SCS from its 2019 campaign.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the domino fear was of identical demands from Bihar and Odisha. Statement 3 is wrong: the YSRCP called the package a 'betrayal' and made SCS its 2019 plank. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2024-26 government stayed in the NDA and sought project funds.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh has stayed in PMFBY without a break since 2019.
st.4: A CCRC gives the tenant ownership rights over the leased land.
st.3: Crop Cultivator Rights Cards are issued under the AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 and are valid for 11 months.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP left PMFBY from Kharif 2020 and rejoined from Kharif 2022. Statement 3 is wrong: CCRCs are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019. Statement 4 is wrong: a CCRC gives no ownership rights.

st.2: 16.2% of APIIC plots were reserved for Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs.
st.3: APIIC's 25% land rebate had no upper cap.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 16.2% of plots were reserved for SC, not ST, entrepreneurs. Statement 3 is wrong: the rebate was capped at Rs 20 lakh.

st.2: The CII Partnership Summit 2025 was held at Amaravati.
st.4: At WEF Davos 2022, Andhra Pradesh signed MoUs with Kia and Hyundai.
st.1: The Global Investors Summit 2023 at Tirupati produced 352 MoUs worth about Rs 13 lakh crore.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: GIS 2023 was held at Visakhapatnam. Statement 2 is wrong: the CII Partnership Summit 2025 was held at Visakhapatnam (610 MoUs, Rs 13.25 lakh crore). Statement 4 is wrong: the Davos 2022 MoUs were with Greenko and ArcelorMittal.

st.4: A gender column has been made optional in the Record of Rights.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the gender column in the RoR has been made mandatory.

st.2: It was criticised for limiting land disputes to the District Court.
st.4: Adoption of the NITI Aayog Model Conclusive Land Titling Act, 2020 is mandatory for all States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was criticised for limiting disputes to the High Court. Statement 4 is wrong: adoption of the Model Act is each State's choice.

st.3: It covers only hospitalisation, with no pre- or post-hospitalisation expenses.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 3 days of pre- and 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses.

st.3: By AUM, UTI remains India's largest mutual fund today.
st.2: The first RBI Mutual Funds Regulations came in 1993.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1993 Mutual Funds Regulations were SEBI's, not the RBI's. Statement 3 is wrong: SBI Mutual Fund, not UTI, is the largest by AUM today.

st.1: Planets shine by reflected sunlight, not by their own light.

x: Both statements are correct.

st.2: Red stars are cooler than yellow stars like the Sun.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.2: The sinking of heavy iron to the Earth's centre is called differentiation.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.2: Latitude values are measured east and west of the Prime Meridian.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: latitude is measured north and south of the Equator (0° to 90°).

st.3: The six-month day and six-month night at the poles are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis as it revolves round the Sun.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.3: Garnet and halite are typical metamorphic minerals.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: halite is an evaporite mineral, not metamorphic.

st.2: In Andhra Pradesh, basalt weathers into laterite soil.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: basalt weathers into black soil, not laterite.

st.3: The Abyssinian plateau is in Arabia.
st.2: The Guiana Highlands are in South America.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Abyssinian plateau is in Ethiopia, Africa.
All four statements are correct.

st.2: The Mekong drains into the South China Sea.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.1: The Bass Strait separates Australia from Tasmania.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.3: They are generally less intense than Bay of Bengal cyclones.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Arabian Sea cyclones are fewer but are becoming more intense.

st.3: Cloudiness is a control (factor) of climate rather than an element.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: cloudiness is an element of weather and climate, not a control.
All three statements are correct.

st.2: The Mizo (Lushai) Hills run north–south.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.3: Podzol is the acidic leached soil of coniferous (taiga) forests.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.2: A coppice is a forest regrown from stump shoots and managed on a short rotation.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.2: Coondapur is in Maharashtra.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Coondapur is in Karnataka, not Maharashtra.

st.2: The IMD has a separate 'extreme drought' category for deficiency above 75%.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IMD has no 'extreme drought' category; above 50% deficiency is severe drought.

st.1: In MADA v. SAIL (2024) the Supreme Court held that royalty is not a tax.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.1: Arabari, the forerunner of Joint Forest Management (1972), is in Odisha.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Arabari is in West Bengal, not Odisha.

st.4: Lonar Lake is a volcanic crater lake.
st.2: The term 'Archaean' was coined by J.D. Dana.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Lonar Lake is a meteorite-impact crater, not volcanic.

st.3: Off-stream closed-loop pumped storage projects still need the concurrence of the Central Electricity Authority.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: off-stream closed-loop pumped storage projects no longer need CEA concurrence.

st.2: India is usually a large exporter of pulses.

st.2: Glaw Lake, India's 101st Ramsar site (August 2026), is in Sikkim.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Glaw Lake is in Arunachal Pradesh (its first Ramsar site); Sukhna Wetland became the 102nd.

st.3: Its products are sold in outlets at Vijayawada and Tirupati.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the outlets are at Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, not Tirupati.

st.2: Its AP pilot is in Mangalagiri mandal, Guntur.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the AP pilot is in Tadikonda mandal, Guntur.

st.2: Conditional patta lands, service inam lands and dotted lands were also removed.
st.3: In partially disputed survey numbers, the entire survey number stays prohibited.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: conditional patta, service inam and dotted lands are still pending with a Group of Ministers. Statement 3 is wrong: only the disputed portion of such a survey number stays prohibited.

st.3: In Phase 3 of Deepam-2, the subsidy is credited in advance to the beneficiaries' accounts.

x: All three statements are correct.

st.4: Old registrations are endorsed free of cost, without any late fee.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: old registrations are endorsed on the licence fee plus a 50% late fee.

st.4: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare alone.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: BBBP (2015) is a joint scheme led by the Ministry of Women and Child Development with Health and Education.

st.3: UFRMP Phase-II is funded entirely by the States.
st.4: Visakhapatnam is the only city in India to have set up a UDMA.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UFRMP Phase-II is funded 90:10 by the Centre and the States. Statement 4 is wrong: Visakhapatnam is the first city in AP but the second in India to set up a UDMA.

st.3: AP's inflation in 2025-26 was the lowest among all States.
st.4: Per capita income is lowest in Alluri Sitharama Raju district.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's 2025-26 inflation (1.39%) was below India's but not the lowest; Telangana's was 0.20%. Statement 4 is wrong: the lowest per capita district figure is Srikakulam's, not Alluri Sitharama Raju's.

st.3: Penukonda was the first capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first capital of Vijayanagara was Anegondi/Hampi, not Penukonda.

st.1: A Danish delegation met APTRANSCO at Rayapudi to design a 33-kV power grid for Amaravati.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the delegation met APCRDA at its Rayapudi headquarters.

st.3: The AP-UAE Food Cluster will use Visakhapatnam and Gangavaram ports.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the cluster will use Krishnapatnam and Kakinada ports.

st.2: PM-SETU is a scheme of the Ministry of Education.
st.4: The Jonnagiri gold mine is being developed by NMDC.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PM-SETU (₹60,000 crore) is under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Statement 4 is wrong: Jonnagiri is a private project (Geomysore Services / Deccan Gold Mines), not NMDC's.

st.2: On NITI Aayog's advice, the Centre builds it and the State funds it.
st.3: The CM ordered completion by July 2027, ahead of the Krishna Pushkaralu 2027.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre funds it (as a national project) while the State builds it. Statement 3 is wrong: completion is tied to the Godavari Pushkaralu 2027, not the Krishna Pushkaralu.

st.3: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Hyderabad as its capital.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Andhra State (1 October 1953) had Kurnool, not Hyderabad, as its capital.

st.2: AP's coastline length was unchanged by the revised measurement.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the revised length is 1,053 km (earlier about 974 km), making AP third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

st.2: Grid integration of the rooftop systems was handled by APTRANSCO.
st.3: It received the SKOCH Award for the implementation of PM-KUSUM.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: grid integration was done by APSPDCL, not APTRANSCO. Statement 3 is wrong: the SKOCH Award was for PM Surya Ghar, not PM-KUSUM.

st.1: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor, with nodes at Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy, is funded by the World Bank.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the VCIC is funded by the Asian Development Bank, not the World Bank.

st.2: It has no deadline for its report.
st.3: Its Chief Engineer (P&M) member is from the NWDA.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is to report within three months. Statement 3 is wrong: the Chief Engineer (P&M) member is from the CWC, not the NWDA.
